title: Water Intake Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Water Intake Calculator: How much water to drink per day. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. How much water to drink per day. Enter your weight and exercise per day and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A practical estimate of daily water needs based on body weight plus extra fluid for exercise. Food provides roughly 20% of total water intake too. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Health & Fitness tools include [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator), [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) and [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator).

## How to use the Water Intake Calculator

Start by entering your weight (kg), then entering your exercise per day (min). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your weight (kg).
2. Enter your exercise per day (min).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

≈ 33 ml per kg of body weight + about 350 ml per 30 minutes of exercise.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 70 kg person who exercises 30 minutes a day needs about 2.7 L of water. Try the same figures in the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Weight: 70 kg, Exercise per day: 30 min), the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) returns Daily water: 2.7 L, Glasses (250 ml): 11, US fl oz: 90. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Pale yellow urine is a good sign of hydration.
- Drink more in hot weather and at altitude.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do coffee and tea count?

Yes, they contribute to fluid intake despite mild diuretic effects. Try it with your own numbers in the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can you drink too much water?

Yes, very large amounts in a short time can cause hyponatraemia. Spread intake through the day. Try it with your own numbers in the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Water Intake Calculator use?

≈ 33 ml per kg of body weight + about 350 ml per 30 minutes of exercise. You can see it in action in the [Water Intake Calculator](/water-intake-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Water Intake Calculator?

Just Weight and Exercise per day. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
